audit.why: FAVOURED at 4/10 fits an 850-range poke champion against a slow melee tank, and the chart already concedes Level 6 to Sion (2/10) where Unstoppable Onslaught arrives. Both layers agree row for row and the mirror recorded no point-2 correction, so I left it.

The spike order on the page is right: Sion's is Level 6 (Unstoppable Onslaught, 140/100/60s over 7500 units, and the cooldown more than halves by rank 3), yours is first item. Mirror recorded no point-3 correction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page asserts in four places that Satchel Charge cancels or interrupts Unstoppable Onslaught. That is an unverifiable claim, and Ziggs's own W flag notes displacement is ignored by unstoppable effects. Separately, Decimating Smash is described as a flat knockup when the knockup is conditional on charge time, and Glory in Death's healing never gets its anti-heal cue.
audit.why: Riot's text on Decimating Smash: 'If he charges for enough time, enemies hit by the swing will also be knocked up and stunned' — a quick release is damage only, on 10/9/8/7/6. Glory in Death: after being killed he reanimates with attacks that 'heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health' — that is the Grievous Wounds window, and it is why raw resistances do not answer him. The mirror explicitly left the Satchel-versus-R question open and escalated it, so I removed the claim rather than reversing it.
audit.corrected: Only a fully charged swing knocks up and stuns; a quick release is damage alone, on 10s at rank 1. Satchel moves YOU off the Onslaught line — plan on dodging, not on stopping the charge. Glory in Death heals off his attacks, so anti-heal is what shortens the reanimation.

notes: Main correction: the page asserted in four separate places that Satchel Charge cancels or interrupts Unstoppable Onslaught.
